headline: High: Cline’s default filesystem/network/tool access can amplify caveman outputs into unsafe actions and data exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and writes to files like CLAUDE.md, while Cline uses MCP plus workspace files and browser/tool outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path through shared files or MCP content, even though caveman has no network egress and the exact bridge is not directly documented.
conditions: IF caveman writes attacker-controlled instructions into shared workspace files or MCP content
IF Cline ingests those files or MCP outputs as prompts without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable shared MCP servers between the agents
Separate their workspaces and file roots
Require explicit human review of any file-based instructions
Add provenance tags to MCP/file content
requires-engineering: enforce prompt/content sanitization at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Cline reads and writes workspace files and can egress broadly to model providers and MCP servers. If sensitive notes land in a shared workspace, Cline can transmit them off-box; caveman’s lack of egress reduces but does not remove the pairwise leakage path.
conditions: IF caveman stores secrets or private notes in files accessible to Cline
IF Cline sends workspace contents to its configured model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep sensitive caveman files outside Cline’s workspace
Turn off Cline MCP servers for shared projects
Use separate OS users or containers
Review and redact memory/session files before opening them in Cline
requires-engineering: add workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses files, while Cline supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem and can write/modify git state. In the same workspace, concurrent writes and git edits can collide by default, creating destructive conflicts and lost work.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace directory
IF both modify the same files or git branch without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Use separate workspace directories
Pause one agent before the other edits git state
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transaction coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content and project notes, and Cline is a coding agent that can act on workspace inputs with shell, browser, and git tools. That makes it plausible for Cline to treat caveman output as authoritative and propagate mistakes into code or commits, though the profiles do not show a fully automated handoff.
conditions: IF caveman output is copied into Cline’s task context or workspace files
IF Cline acts on that output without independent verification
mitigations: Require source checks before acting on caveman output
Keep caveman outputs in a review-only folder
Have Cline cite file provenance before edits
Use a human approval step for commits and external actions
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the evidence only shows caveman touching session logs/memory files and Cline handling model-provider API keys and workspace files. No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so the compliance risk is limited to local handling gaps rather than a proven breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman files that Cline can access
IF Cline’s configured provider or MCP server has retention rules incompatible with that data class
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces
Review provider retention settings
Separate secrets from project notes
Document data-class handling rules
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
